| 4 | BOB@x.com | 20 | 2 |
| 5 | cy@x.com | NULL | 1 |
| 6 | cy@x.com | 7 | 6 |

Dialect: standard SQL, PostgreSQL semantics (NULL sorts as largest, integer / integer truncates).

```sql
WITH c AS (
  SELECT LOWER(TRIM(email)) AS em, NULLIF(amt, 'n/a') AS a, ts,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY LOWER(TRIM(email))
                            ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn
  FROM raw
)
SELECT SUM(CAST(a AS INTEGER)) FROM c WHERE rn = 1;
```

What does the query return?

rubric.text: Normalising email merges Ann/ann and Bob/BOB
ROW_NUMBER by ts DESC keeps the latest row per email: ids 2, 3, 6
NULLIF turns 'n/a' into NULL; SUM = 15 + 7

solution:
LOWER(TRIM(...)) groups ' Ann@x.com ' with 'ann@x.com' and so on (cleaning).
rn = 1 per email by latest ts: ann id 2 (15), bob id 3 ('n/a'), cy id 6 (7) (window).
NULLIF makes 'n/a' NULL; SUM skips it (null).
Sum = 15 + 7 = 22.
hints: Latest row per person, then deal with 'n/a'.

prompt:
Table $A$ has 2,000 rows and $B$ has 500 rows. A query filters $A$ to 10% of its rows with a WHERE, then joins to $B$ on a key. Plan 1 is a nested loop (every filtered $A$ row against every $B$ row). Plan 2 builds a hash table on $B$ ($|B|$ operations) and probes it once per filtered $A$ row. Count one comparison or one insert/probe as one operation.

How many times more operations does Plan 1 use than Plan 2? Give a decimal.

rubric.text: Filter first: 200 rows of A
Nested loop: 200 x 500 = 100,000
Hash: 500 build + 200 probe = 700

solution:
The WHERE reduces A to 200 rows before the join (select).
Nested loop: 200 x 500 = 100,000 comparisons (complexity).
Hash join: 500 inserts + 200 probes = 700 operations (joins).
Ratio = 100,000 / 700 = 142.9.
hints: Apply the filter before sizing the join.

prompt:
A table has $n=10^6$ rows. Query X sorts all rows once (`OVER (ORDER BY v)`). Query Y partitions into 1,000 equal groups and sorts each (`OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v)`). Model a sort of $m$ rows as $m\log_2 m$ comparisons and ignore everything else.

How many times more comparisons does Query X use than Query Y?

rubric.text: X cost = $n\log_2 n$ with $\log_2 10^6\approx19.93$
Y cost = 1000 sorts of 1000 rows: $10^6\log_2 1000$

solution:
X: $10^6\log_2 10^6 \approx 19.9\times10^6$ (complexity).
Y: 1,000 groups, each $10^3\log_2 10^3$, total $10^6\log_2 10^3\approx 10.0\times10^6$ (window).
The $10^6$ factors cancel.
Ratio $=\log_2 10^6/\log_2 10^3 = 6/3 = 2$ (agg of costs).
hints: The partition count changes the log term only.
